title: Swap compatibility of arbitrary derived tensor evaluation arrows
statement: Fix P as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let B,Y,Z be schemes with maps to Spec(k), a:Y→B and b:Z→B. In the intrinsic ordinary unbounded categories take arbitrary F,G∈D(B), H∈D(Y), J∈D(Z), and arrows e:P_a F→H, d:P_b G→J. Use pairEvaluation, swapPull and swapTensor from [def-pur-finite-proper-product-maps], including their actual canonical tensor and pullback compositors. Then P_c(sigma(F,G));swapPull_(G⊗F);P_s(pairEvaluation_(b,a)(d,e));swapTensor_(H,J) = pairEvaluation_(a,b)(e,d), where c=t;b and s:Y×_B Z→Z×_B Y is the actual pullback symmetry. No direct image, exchange, projection, adjunction counit, or properness is used.

proof.text: Expand pairEvaluation and swapTensor. Naturality of the canonical pullback tensor comparison moves the tensor of the arbitrary arrows past that comparison. Its composition law combines the successive tensor comparisons.

proof.text: Pullback composition and the two projection equations s;r′=t, s;t′=r identify the two projection factors. The signed-braiding compatibility of the tensor comparison moves the input symmetry through pullback. Naturality of the signed output symmetry moves e and d through it; involutivity cancels the remaining two symmetries. The Koszul signs are those of the specified derived signed symmetry throughout.

lean.statement: theorem finiteProductEvaluationSwap (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {B Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (a : Y ⟶ B) (b : Z ⟶ B) (sB : B ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) (sZ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) (F G : D P B) (H : D P Y) (J : D P Z) (e : (pull P a).obj F ⟶ H) (d : (pull P b).obj G ⟶ J) : (pull P (pullback.snd a b ≫ b)).map (sigma P B F G).hom ≫ (swapPull P a b).hom.app ((tensor P B).obj (G, F)) ≫ (pull P (pullbackSymmetry a b).hom).map (pairEvaluation P b a sB sY G F J H d e) ≫ swapTensor P a b sY sZ H J = pairEvaluation P a b sB sZ F G H J e d
